# Jev on a synthetic survey

> An independent evaluation of TypeSafe's Jev (jev-1.13.0), a decision-only model that returns a probability per option natively, against GPT-4.1 asked to state one, as synthetic survey respondents on the public Twin-2K-500 benchmark. Same 300 respondents, 108 questions, 16 behavioral-economics tasks. Asked each yes/no question as a Noul, Jev leads GPT-4.1 probabilities on all six measures at $4.02 against about $136; plain GPT-4.1 hard answers score about two points higher on accuracy and return no distribution. Asked as a two-option Choice, Jev trails on the distribution gap (0.1985 against 0.1789). No affiliation with TypeSafe or OpenAI; self-funded.

## Start here

- [The essay](https://jjd-lab.github.io/jev-synthetic-survey/): the result, the figures and the walkthrough, as one page

## Survey track (what transfers to any model on this benchmark)

- [Dataset and instrument](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/survey/01-dataset-and-instrument.md): Twin-2K-500, the 108 scored questions, the human ceiling
- [Metrics](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/survey/02-metrics.md): every measure, defined once
- [Grounding panel](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/survey/03-grounding-panel.md): what persona content buys, GPT-4.1 over all 2,058 respondents
- [Elicitation effects](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/survey/04-elicitation-effects.md): how you ask changes what the model answers
- [Segment diversity](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/survey/05-segment-diversity.md): do synthetic demographic segments differ the way real ones do
- [Limitations](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/survey/06-limitations.md)

## Jev track (the verdict on this model)

- [Question and criteria](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/jev/01-question-and-criteria.md): what was asked, and the two tests written down before the runs
- [The planned comparison](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/jev/02-planned-comparison.md): Jev Choice against GPT-4.1, and the verdict
- [The Noul follow-up](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/jev/03-noul-follow-up.md): re-asking the yes/no questions as a single probability
- [Price sensitivity](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/jev/04-price-sensitivity.md)
- [Option descriptions](https://github.com/jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey/blob/main/docs/jev/05-option-descriptions.md)
